actions.reason:
I found no change to the decode path that is likely to reach the 1% minimum, so I am submitting nothing.

What the code already does:
- RegexTokenizer.decode and BasicTokenizer.decode build the id-to-bytes lookup list once and cache it, along with the decoded text for recent id lists.
- In the benchmark, every decode call after the first round is a cache hit. It costs one list comparison in C plus one dict equality check on the vocab.
- The regex module is imported only on first use. Loading the model file happens once per process. The joins are already one batched b"".join over a list comprehension, so the suggested "batch byte concatenation and cache the id-to-bytes mapping" is already in place.

What was tried earlier on this lineage:
- Replacing the per-id lookup with map(list.__getitem__) measured decode_ir at ratio 1.1104.
- Adding a min() check so the per-id sign branch could be dropped measured ratio 1.0276.
- Both made decode slower than the required 0.99 and were dropped.

What I checked this time: the remaining library work per call is the cache-hit comparisons and the one-off first-round join and decode. Both are small next to the fixed cost of starting the interpreter and generating inputs. I don't have a credible edit that saves 1% without weakening the mutation-safety checks on the cache, so I did not spend an evaluation on a guess.
